title: What are files and folders?
summary: The two things everything on a computer is made of, and what a path is.

steps.title: Files
steps.say: A **file** is one saved thing on a computer: a photo, a song, a school paper, or a piece of code. Every file has a **name**, so you can find it again.

board.code:
robot.png      a picture
song.mp3       a song
notes.txt      some plain words
Main.java      a piece of code

marks.label: a file with code in it

steps.title: Names have endings
steps.say: The part after the dot is the **extension**. It tells you (and the computer) what kind of file it is. The part before the dot is whatever name you choose.

marks.label: the extension: what kind of file

board.caption: `.txt` is text, `.java` is Java code, `.png` is a picture.

steps.title: Folders
steps.say: A **folder** holds files, like a drawer or a binder. Folders keep things organized. And a folder can hold other folders, as many levels deep as you like.

board.caption: Folders are written with a / after the name here.

steps.title: A project
steps.say: A **project** is one folder with everything for a program inside it. When the editor opened, it opened your project folder. Everything you see in the Explorer is inside it.

steps.title: Paths
steps.say: A **path** is a file's address: the folders you walk through to reach it, separated by slashes.

steps.title: Why this matters
steps.say: Code isn't magic: it's words typed into files. Programmers spend a lot of time making, naming, moving and finding files. So let's practice. Try **Make a folder and a file** next.
